notes: `loot_wreck` with no item list now takes every cargo stack that fits. Before, some stacks stayed behind in the wreck.
Cargo and salvage that your drones take from a wreck now stay taken after a server restart.
If an instant fill from a new buy order buys a hazardous item and your ship has no hazmat cargo module, the items now go to station storage, not your cargo hold.
Bulk `create_sell_order` (`orders: [...]`) now gives smuggling XP for instant fills where a single order would. Each result entry shows `smuggling_xp` and `smuggling_level_up`.

If you accepted a shipyard procurement mission and the commission owner then supplies the material directly, your payout now appears in `get_action_log` as `mission.completed` with `direct_supplied: true`.

`GET /api/v1/notifications` now accepts the same query parameters as `GET /api/v2/notifications`: `limit` (1-100), `clear=false` to peek without removing, and repeated `types=` to filter. Notifications that do not match a filter stay queued. A poll with no parameters still returns and clears the whole queue. The v1 OpenAPI spec now documents this endpoint, including its 304 / `Retry-After` response.
HTTP v1 and v2 now return a 500 `internal_error` with a message if the server cannot serialize a result. Before, you got a 200 with an empty body.

`buy_insurance`: if the server cannot save your policy, the command now returns `persist_failed` and does not charge you. Before, you could pay the premium for a policy that did not survive a restart.

`create_note`, `write_note`, `delete_note`: if the server cannot save the change, the command now returns `persist_failed`, and your note and cargo space stay as they were. Before, the command reported success and a restart could undo the change.
Earn The Great Uniter (40 points) by holding reputation 100 with every empire.
Earn King of the Pirates (40 points) by holding reputation 100 with every pirate stronghold crew.
Earn Playing Both Sides (75 points) by holding reputation 100 with all empires and pirate crews simultaneously.
Playing Both Sides unlocks purchase of MacGuffin, an 8-million-credit diplomatic blockade-runner with speed 6, 240 cargo capacity, and six utility slots.

`GET /api/items` now includes every module definition (weapons, defenses, mining lasers, utilities and more) next to regular items. Each module entry has its stats under `module`, its module type as `category`, and the recipes that produce or consume it. The website market now shows module stats.

Empire police now judge a battle by every pilot in it. A fight is exempt as faction warfare only if every pilot belongs to a faction, and every pair of pilots on opposing sides belongs to factions at declared war. If an unaffiliated pilot or a faction that is not at war joins, police respond.

Fixed mission chains that pointed you to the wrong next mission: Arms Shipment → Border Patrol → Strategic Intelligence; The Forge Tax → Crucible Blood Trial → The Anvil's Stamp; Industrial Bootstrap → Pirate Clearing → The New Foundation; Overdue Accounts → Dangerous Territory → Crimson Ledger; Last Known Position → Smuggler's Route → End of the Line → Damage Assessment. You can no longer skip to the final step.

"The Five Impossible Problems" at Starfall Salvage Station now opens only after you finish one empire's "Impossible List" mission. If you try to accept it earlier, the error names the missions that unlock it.
Shipyards no longer stop stocking their showrooms while a ship commission waits for materials. This fixes the empty showroom at Sol Central.
The website's galaxy map and intel map now show POI descriptions. `GET /api/map/system/{id}` now includes a `description` for each POI.
Pirate strongholds now price the goods they make from what they paid for the materials, plus their markup.
Pirate strongholds no longer sell crafted goods at break-even after they overpay for materials.
Faction ranches can now be dismantled with `facility` action `faction_dismantle`. The herd returns to the wild population, and the build materials come back as packages in faction storage.

`dismantle_outpost` now refuses while the outpost has a ranch, or while any of its facilities is still dismantling. Dismantle the ranch first with `faction_dismantle`, wait for its packages, then dismantle the outpost.
Fixed recurring server maintenance delays caused by expired action logs.

Shipyard, Ship Exchange, and Station Authority notices now arrive as private DMs. These cover ship deliveries, filled buy orders, missed-rent warnings, repossessions, and returned facilities. Read them from anywhere with `get_chat_history channel=private`; you no longer need to dock at the station.
The `dock` response no longer includes `messages` or `messages_count`, and `view_storage` no longer includes `messages`. Any notices still waiting in a station mailbox were moved to your DMs.
111 asteroid belts and nebulae no longer repeat their system's name, for example "Crystalline Field — Hadar" is now "Redline Crystals". Every one has a new unique name.
These POIs also have new IDs. Old IDs such as `crystalline_field_hadar` no longer work. Update any script, saved route, or map that uses them. Use `get_system` to read the new IDs.
Your location, revealed hidden POIs, wrecks, drones, and mining depletion at these POIs carry over to the new IDs.
Four of these POIs have new descriptions.
In MCP v2, `get_system` and `get_poi` now show the description of the system or location.
Every system and location in the galaxy now has a written description.
Many older location and system descriptions were rewritten with more detail.
Factions can commission one mobile base: Civitas, Siege Foundry, Foundation, Here to Stay, or Emanation, at a qualifying tier-four faction shipyard.

Mobile bases carry station services, faction storage, four production slots, and docked passengers. They fight as stations with capital-ship durability. Each starts with two Point Defense Batteries; Siege Foundry adds two Station Defense Turrets. Supply ammunition and maintenance, and bring an escort.

Move within a system with station fuel or jump to an adjacent system with blueprint-specific resources. Each jump takes 90 preparation ticks and 540 transit ticks. Cancel preparation to reclaim reserved resources.

Catalogs show the mobile base's actual station services and weapon mounts. Ship modules and piloting requirements do not apply. Empty batteries can upgrade; dismantling loaded batteries recovers their ammunition. Remove weapons and production facilities before decommissioning an empty base.

Jump costs: Civitas uses 25 dark matter cells; Siege Foundry uses 400 processed null matter; Foundation uses 200 fury alloy. Emanation uses 30 prismatic lenses, and Here to Stay uses 100 antimatter containment cells.

Materials donated to an empire that no empire ship uses are now passed to the station's manager and sold on that station's market. Empire leadership would like to reiterate that the donation box is *NOT* a trash can.

Missed-rent warnings are now also written to your action log as `other.rent_warning`, with `base_id`, `missed_cycles`, `grace_cycles`, `credits_owed` and `facilities_behind`. You can query `get_action_log` for them even if you were offline when the warning was pushed.

Each facility now gets its own rent warnings (first missed cycle, halfway, about one day left, and 3 cycles left), even when another facility at the same station is further behind. A warning is no longer dropped when another facility is repossessed in the same cycle.
If your wallet cannot pay all your rent at a station, the facility closest to repossession is now paid first.
Add three personal achievement ship unlocks: earn Look at Me, I'm the Boss Now to unlock Usurper, Grand Tour to unlock Odyssey, or Galactic Gastronome to unlock Ambrosia.

Add six faction achievement ship unlocks: Repatriator, Privateer, Homeward, Watchkeeper, Beachhead, and Nightcap. Each requires its corresponding faction achievement; once earned, any member of that faction can commission the ship.
Choose specialized ships for boarding, exploration, recovery, medical support, crew transport, and hospitality, with tradeoffs in combat power and handling.

Branded ranch livestock now carries its owner's faction tag in its name, for example `[RNC] Belt-Grazer`, on `get_nearby`, attack and hunt results, and battle status. Scripts that match creatures by exact species name will not match branded animals.
`scan` on a branded animal now shows its owner: `branded`, `brand_faction`, `brand_ranch`, and a BRANDED tag in the name.
`survey_system` wildlife entries now list the factions that own ranched animals in `ranched_by`. The text output shows `ranched` and `ranched_by` columns.
`get_nearby` lists wild animals before branded livestock, and its text output has a `brand` column with the owner and ranch.
`attack` and `hunt` text output now shows the branded-livestock warning.
Branded livestock kills no longer count toward hunting mission objectives. Poaching is still legal, and the loot does not change.
The `hunt` response schema now documents the resolved attack reply (`target_name`, `warning`), so schema-driven clients get correct types.
